records.title: [Unloading fish at "T" wharf, Boston, Mass.]
records.creator: Detroit Publishing Co., publisher; individual photographer not identified in the record
notes: Title from jacket.
1685 on negative.
Detroit Publishing Co. no. 033317.
Gift; State Historical Society of Colorado; 1949.
The catalogue's later summary names the outboard schooner Stranger (C. Seavey, 2026); no additional vessel history is inferred here.
records.description: Fishing vessels at Boston's T wharf, dated 1900–1910 in the catalogue. This is a different place and record from the Gloucester fish-handling photograph, not a before-and-after pair.
records.alt: Fishing schooners and dense rigging beside Boston's T wharf, with dock buildings across the water.
nativeNotes: Gift; State Historical Society of Colorado; 1949.
nativeSummary: Photo shows three schooners. The outboard schooner is Stranger. (The name is on her stern.) Built in Essex, MA, in 1883 by Moses Adams. She fished out of Gloucester, but like many of the Gloucester fleet often offloaded in Boston.  (C. Seavey, 2026)
